overview: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world, stretching across Central Asia. Its capital is Astana and its largest city is Almaty. Kazakhstan became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991. It is rich in oil, gas and minerals, and the Baikonur Cosmodrome, from which the first person was launched into space in 1961, is on its territory.

geography.text: Much of Kazakhstan is flat steppe: vast grassland and semi-desert. Mountains rise in the south-east, around Almaty, and the west borders the Caspian Sea. Lake Balkhash in the east is half fresh water and half salt water, and the Aral Sea, which Kazakhstan shares with Uzbekistan, has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s.

history.text: The steppes of Kazakhstan were home to nomadic peoples for thousands of years, and the Kazakh Khanate formed in the 1400s. Russia took control in the 1700s and 1800s. Under Soviet rule, a famine in the early 1930s killed more than a million Kazakhs, and the Soviet Union tested nuclear weapons at Semipalatinsk. Kazakhstan became independent in 1991.

events.title: Kazakh Khanate
events.text: The first Kazakh state is founded.

events.title: Russian protection
events.text: Kazakh leaders begin accepting Russian protection.

events.title: Famine
events.text: Forced collectivisation causes a famine that kills over a million people.

events.title: Nuclear tests
events.text: The Soviet Union carries out its first nuclear test at Semipalatinsk.

events.title: New capital
events.text: The capital moves from Almaty to Astana.
